title: Ohio State signs record $17M annual jersey patch deal with JPMorganChase
dek: Ohio State signed a partnership with JPMorganChase that places jersey patches on all 36 athletic teams and generates nearly $17 million annually for the athletic program. The deal is believed to be one of the largest non-apparel corporate sponsorships in college sports and exceeds many NBA jersey patch deals.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Ohio State signed a corporate partnership with JPMorganChase for jersey patches across all 36 teams generating nearly $17 million per year, believed to be one of the largest non-apparel corporate deals in college sports.
bottom_line: The $17 million annual benchmark set by Ohio State's JPMorganChase deal establishes a new revenue threshold for jersey patches in college athletics. Other major programs will likely test whether comparable or higher valuations are achievable with Fortune 500 companies, and the CFP's ongoing deliberation on postseason patch eligibility could unlock additional revenue streams. Watch whether other major conferences and schools announce competing jersey patch deals in the coming months.
body: Ohio State entered a corporate partnership with JPMorganChase that includes jersey patches on all 36 of the Buckeyes' athletic teams and will generate nearly $17 million per year for the athletic program, according to ESPN's reporting.

The deal is believed to be one of the biggest non-apparel corporate sponsorships in college sports. The yearly income generated by the jersey patches is expected to be an industry leader and is bigger than many NBA jersey patch deals, per ESPN.

The partnership includes NIL opportunities for athletes in addition to the jersey patch component, according to ESPN's reporting. Ohio State athletic director Ross Bjork stated in comments reported by ESPN: "JPMorganChase is a global brand with deep roots in Ohio, making them a natural partner that shares our commitment to innovation, excellence and long-term community impact." Bjork added: "Together, we have built a comprehensive and historic partnership that reflects the strong commercial strength of the Ohio State Athletics identity and the broader college athletics landscape. This relationship creates meaningful opportunities for our student-athletes that support the sustained excellence and competitiveness of our athletic programs, while honoring the tradition and values of Ohio State."

Uniform patches were approved in January by Division I leaders as a mechanism to generate millions in revenue for athletic departments. Under the new rules, teams can place up to two patches of no more than 4 square inches on uniforms for regular-season games, in addition to logos already allowed for uniform manufacturers, per ESPN.
The College Football Playoff has been exploring how to allow patches for that sport's postseason competition, according to ESPN's reporting.
